_about: Hand-assigned treatment labels for 40 citation edges of index/citations.jsonl, read by scripts/treatment_audit.py. Sampled 10 per predicted label with random.Random(358) from the labelling produced by nyaya/authority/treatment.py. Each label is my reading of the sentence window, assigned before looking at whether the classifier agreed. Annotator: Rakshit (M1).

_notes.33581: Borderline: the edge's cite_string is 'AIR 1992 SC 165' but the window names 'AIR 1992 SC 196' - an OCR digit transposition in the same citation. The sentence does declare that cited decision per incuriam, so I score it correct; a stricter annotator would score it wrong and the overruled precision would read 9/10.
_notes.67110: The classifier says 'followed' from an 'affirmed' cue 425 characters away, inside a long sentencing discussion. The cited case is merely referred to, so the truth is 'mentioned'. This is the one error in the 40.
_notes.21390: Shared list disposition: 'A; B; C ... - relied on' applies to every citation in the list, which is why the followed cue is uncapped by distance.
_notes.13129: Not in the sample, but kept here as the documented limitation: see scripts/treatment_audit.py --limitation.

limitation_case.why: Negation scope is approximated by a character window (NEGATION_WINDOW_CHARS = 80) instead of a syntactic parse. Here 'could not be continued by his legal representatives' is part of the proposition the cited case held, not a negation of the following 'overruled'. The window sees 'not' 24 characters before the cue and suppresses a real overruling, so the edge is labelled 'mentioned'.
limitation_case.video_beat: show-a-limitation-live: run `python -m nyaya.authority.treatment explain --edge 13129` and read the sentence aloud
